Tweedieverse

Differential analysis of omics data using Tweedie models.

Tweedieverse fits one model per feature, supports multiple covariates and optional random effects, and returns association tables with effect estimates and adjusted p-values. It accepts microbiome, single-cell, bulk RNA-seq, and other omics measurements through Bioconductor containers.

Input · Quick start · Output · Model options · Multi-omics · Documentation

Installation

Once Tweedieverse is available in your Bioconductor version, install it with:

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("Tweedieverse")

See the Bioconductor installation guide for R/Bioconductor version compatibility and setup.

Install the development version from GitHub:

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("himelmallick/Tweedieverse")

Input

Supply a container whose assay has features in rows and samples in columns. Sample covariates belong in colData; sample identifiers are used to align the assay and metadata. Select the assay with assay_name (default "counts").

Data / domain Preferred container Default normalization
Microbiome / "microbiome" TreeSummarizedExperiment TSS
Single-cell / "single_cell" SingleCellExperiment SCRAN
Bulk RNA-seq / "bulk_rnaseq" SummarizedExperiment TMM
Other omics / "custom" A supported SummarizedExperiment-like container MEDIAN

For multiple assays, use a MultiAssayExperiment (see below). To use your own count matrix and metadata, first wrap them in a supported container. Plain feature tables, matrices, lists, and file paths are not accepted as input_features. An optional input_metadata data frame can override container metadata.

Quick start

This example uses packaged PBMC3k UMI counts: 20 genes across 60 CD4/CD8 cells. The library-size column was calculated from all source genes before subsetting.

library(Tweedieverse)

umi_sce <- readRDS(system.file(
    "extdata", "umi_sce.rds", package = "Tweedieverse"
))

fit <- Tweedieverse(
    input_features = umi_sce,
    output = NULL,
    assay_name = "counts",
    domain = "single_cell",
    fixed_effects = "CellType",
    reference = "CellType,CD8",
    scale_factor = "library_size",
    tweedie_p = 1,
    return_all = TRUE
)

head(fit)
discoveries <- subset(fit, !is.na(qval) & qval <= 0.05)

The example fixes p = 1 to illustrate the Poisson variance case. Leaving tweedie_p = NULL estimates a compound Poisson-gamma power for each feature. This is a cell-type illustration from one donor; population-level inference requires biological replication and an appropriate study design.

Output

For a single assay, Tweedieverse() returns a data.frame, ordered by q-value. By default, it returns associations with qval <= max_significance (0.05). Use return_all = TRUE to inspect the full available table, including with output = NULL. Missing q-values are excluded from significance selection.

Columns Meaning
feature, metadata, value Feature, covariate, and tested level or predictor
coef, stderr Coefficient and standard error on the model’s link scale
pval, qval Test p-value and adjusted p-value; correction defaults to BH
base.model, tweedie.index Model label and fitted or fixed variance power
N, N.not.zero, percent.zero Aligned sample count, positive measurements, and rounded percentage of zeros

In the quick start, CellType coefficients compare CD4 with CD8. With the log link, a positive coefficient indicates a higher fitted mean in CD4 cells, and exp(coef) is the mean ratio at equal library size. Continuous covariates are standardized by default; use standardize = FALSE for their original units.

Set output to a directory to write all_results.tsv, significant_results.tsv, logs, and model-index plots. Add plot_heatmap = TRUE or plot_scatter = TRUE for optional association plots. output = NULL creates no output directory or files.

Model options

Variance power

tweedie_p Model choice
NULL Estimate a feature-specific compound Poisson-gamma power, 1 < p < 2, for non-negative data
0 Gaussian case; MaAsLin2 linear modeling by default
1 Poisson variance case
Between 1 and 2 Fixed compound Poisson-gamma power
2 Gamma variance case
3 Inverse Gaussian variance case

The default link is log. At p = 0, the package uses an identity link and disables log offsets. Negative measurements require p = 0; an unspecified power resolves to zero when negative values remain after filtering. Powers between zero and one are undefined. See the function help for other supported powers and random-effect restrictions.

At p = 0, use Maaslin2_run = FALSE to select the Tweedie GLM implementation. Optional p0_transform choices are NONE, CLR, RCLR, LOG, and ARC_SIGNED_SQRT. These operate on an analysis copy of the feature matrix.

Normalization and offsets

Normalization estimates sample size factors and enters them as offset(log(size_factor)); it does not divide or replace the response matrix. Choose a strategy with normalization, supply a colData column with scale_factor, or disable offsets with adjust_offset = FALSE. A supplied scale_factor overrides the normalization strategy.

For already scaled relative abundances, use normalization = "NONE". Filtering uses abd_threshold, prev_threshold, and var_threshold; entropy_threshold controls metadata filtering.

Sparse assays are preserved through filtering and Tweedie fitting. MaAsLin2, the edgeR TMM backend, selected transformations, and association plots can require dense representations; see the tutorial for details.

Optional analyses

  • Presence/absence: set run_presence_absence_model = TRUE to combine abundance and prevalence evidence using a Cauchy combination test. By default, prevalence fitting requires at least three detected and three undetected samples; adjust this with min_presence_absence_count. Below either minimum, pval_presence is missing and the abundance p-value is used directly. Exact component p-values of 0 and 1 combine to 0. Component results are retained alongside the joint p-value and q-value; coef remains the abundance effect.
  • Median comparison: for relative-abundance analyses, enable median_comparison = TRUE to test effects against a covariate-specific median. Set median_comparison_seed for reproducible Monte Carlo calculations. A supplied seed restores the previous RNG state afterward.
  • Study design and execution: use fixed_effects, random_effects, and reference to specify the design, method_args for engine-specific options, and BPPARAM for BiocParallel execution. The default backend is serial.

Multi-omics

A MultiAssayExperiment returns a named list of association tables, each with an omics column. Layers are fitted independently and q-values are adjusted within each layer. Sample alignment uses sampleMap.

mae <- readRDS(system.file(
    "extdata", "franzosa_example_mae.rds", package = "Tweedieverse"
))

multi_fit <- Tweedieverse(
    input_features = mae,
    output = NULL,
    assay_name = "abundance",
    fixed_effects = c("diseaseCat_clean", "Age"),
    domain = c(
        taxaAbundanceProfile = "microbiome",
        harmonizedMetaboliteProfile = "custom"
    ),
    normalization = c(
        taxaAbundanceProfile = "NONE",
        harmonizedMetaboliteProfile = "MEDIAN"
    ),
    return_all = TRUE
)

names(multi_fit)
head(multi_fit$taxaAbundanceProfile)

Most arguments accept a shared value or named values keyed by layer. Use a named list when a layer needs NULL, such as a mix of estimated and fixed powers.

Documentation and example data

The tutorial covers microbiome abundances, UMI and non-UMI single-cell data, pseudobulk aggregation with muscat, bulk RNA-seq with airway, multi-omics analysis, result interpretation, and visualization.

vignette("Tweedieverse", package = "Tweedieverse")
?Tweedieverse

Packaged examples run without downloads. See the data provenance and licences and preparation instructions for their sources and reconstruction steps.
